title: In-Memory OLTP
description: Use memory-optimized tables and natively compiled procedures for latch-free, high-concurrency workloads.

data.text: In-Memory OLTP stores a table entirely in memory and uses optimistic, row-version-based concurrency instead of locks and latches. Writers never block readers, and readers never block writers. SQL Server 2014 introduced the feature; since SQL Server 2016 you can alter memory-optimized tables and use them in more workloads. It is designed for high-contention OLTP, not for analytics.

items: MEMORY_OPTIMIZED = ON stores the table in memory; there is no page buffer pool.
DURABILITY = SCHEMA_AND_DATA persists data in checkpoint files and the log; SCHEMA_ONLY loses data on restart.
Hash indexes are ideal for point lookups; range indexes are ideal for range scans and sorting.
Natively compiled procedures compile T-SQL to machine code and avoid the interpreted query path.
Memory is not unlimited: the table must fit in the memory-optimized filegroup and is subject to a resource governor pool.

data.title: A schema-only session cache
data.content: The primary key uses a hash index sized for the expected number of distinct session ids. A second range index supports cleanup by expiry time.
data.code:
CREATE TABLE dbo.SessionCache
(
    SessionId UNIQUEIDENTIFIER NOT NULL
        CONSTRAINT PK_SessionCache PRIMARY KEY NONCLUSTERED
        HASH WITH (BUCKET_COUNT = 1048576),
    UserId    INT NOT NULL,
    Payload   NVARCHAR(4000) NOT NULL,
    ExpiresAt DATETIME2 NOT NULL,
    INDEX IX_SessionCache_ExpiresAt NONCLUSTERED (ExpiresAt)
)
WITH
(
    MEMORY_OPTIMIZED = ON,
    DURABILITY = SCHEMA_ONLY
);

data.title: Bucket count matters
data.text: A hash index with too few buckets turns into long collision chains and loses its advantage. Size the bucket count for the peak number of rows, rounded up to a power of two. You can inspect and change it with `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER INDEX ... REBUILD WITH (BUCKET_COUNT = ...)`.

data.title: A natively compiled lookup
data.content: Natively compiled procedures can only access memory-optimized tables and must be schema-bound. The isolation level is declared once in BEGIN ATOMIC.
data.code:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.GetActiveSession
    @SessionId UNIQUEIDENTIFIER
WITH NATIVE_COMPILATION, SCHEMABINDING
AS
BEGIN ATOMIC
WITH
(
    TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL = SNAPSHOT,
    LANGUAGE = N'us_english'
)
    SELECT UserId, Payload, ExpiresAt
    FROM dbo.SessionCache
    WHERE SessionId = @SessionId
      AND ExpiresAt > SYSUTCDATETIME();
END;

data.title: Limitations to know before you commit
data.text: Memory-optimized tables do not support all T-SQL features: foreign keys between memory-optimized and disk-based tables, `TRUNCATE TABLE`, some data types, and cross-database transactions have restrictions. Schema changes require special handling. The table also counts against the memory-optimized resource pool, so a runaway table can starve the instance.

data.title: Find memory-optimized tables by memory usage
data.content: Use the XTP memory DMV to see how much each table and its indexes consume. Compare against the resource pool limit to catch growth early.
data.code:
SELECT
    OBJECT_NAME(t.object_id) AS table_name,
    t.durability_desc,
    s.memory_used_by_table_kb,
    s.memory_used_by_indexes_kb
FROM sys.dm_db_xtp_table_memory_stats AS s
JOIN sys.tables AS t
    ON t.object_id = s.object_id
ORDER BY s.memory_used_by_table_kb DESC;

data.title: Interview angle: when is In-Memory OLTP the right answer?
data.text: It is the right answer for very high-concurrency OLTP with short transactions, hot rows, and contention on latches — session state, counters, queues, and similar workloads. It is the wrong answer for large analytical scans, tables that do not fit in memory, or workloads that need the full T-SQL surface. In an interview, say what problem it solves (latch and lock contention) and what it costs (memory, limitations, operational complexity).

data.title: In-Memory OLTP Key Points
points: Memory-optimized tables use optimistic concurrency, so readers and writers do not block each other.
DURABILITY = SCHEMA_AND_DATA persists data; SCHEMA_ONLY is for caches and session state.
Hash indexes favor point lookups; range indexes favor scans and ordering.
Natively compiled procedures are schema-bound and run compiled code.
Size bucket counts for peak rows and monitor memory with sys.dm_db_xtp_table_memory_stats.
Use it for high-contention OLTP, not for analytics or tables larger than memory.
